q: What is the main difference between a Foundry agent and a plain model deployment?
opts: An agent is simply a bigger model
An agent adds instructions and tools on top of a model, so it can find information and take actions
An agent does not use a model
An agent is a billing plan
exp: A model deployment answers prompts, while an agent wraps a model with stored instructions and tools such as file search or API calls, so it can ground answers and act. An agent is not a bigger model, it always relies on a model, and it is not a billing plan.

ctx: A travel company's agent answers questions from the company's brochures and must also check live flight prices from a partner's REST API.
q: Which tool lets the agent get the live flight prices?
opts: An OpenAPI tool or a function for the partner's flight API
exp: Live prices come from the partner's API, so the agent needs an action tool, such as an OpenAPI tool or a function, that calls it. File search only covers the uploaded brochures, code interpreter runs Python in a sandbox, and image generation creates pictures.

q: For each of the following statements about agent tools, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Grounding with Bing Search can read the company's private intranet for an agent.
File search answers from documents such as PDF and Word files that you upload.
Code interpreter can return text and numbers, while charts need the image generation tool.
exp: No for the first: Bing grounding searches the public web; private content needs file search or a connected search index. Yes for the second: common document formats can be uploaded for file search. No for the third: code interpreter can generate charts and other files as output.

q: Match each agent problem to the change that fixes it. Each fix can be used once or not at all.
items: The agent makes up answers about company policy
The agent sends emails without asking anyone
The agent cannot answer questions about today's events
The agent's answers are much too long
targets: Add a length rule to the instructions
Add file search over the policy documents and tell the agent to use them
Require human approval before the email tool runs
exp: Made-up policy answers need grounding in the policy documents, unapproved emails need an approval step, current events need web grounding, and long answers need a length rule. Quota affects throughput and fixes none of these problems.

q: Complete the sentence about creating an agent in the Foundry portal.
tpl: You give the agent a name, choose a {0}, and write its {1}.
exp: An agent needs a model deployment to do its reasoning and instructions that define its behavior; tools can be added afterward. Storage accounts, regions, invoices and passwords are not what you set when you create an agent.

q: You are testing a new customer support agent in the Foundry portal. Which TWO test prompts are most useful? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: A request that the agent should refuse or redirect
exp: Typical questions show whether the agent does its job, and requests it should refuse show whether its rules and safety behavior work. A single greeting, random characters and endless repetition reveal little about how the agent will perform with real users.

q: An agent with code interpreter will analyze a spreadsheet that contains customer email addresses. Which practice is best?
opts: Upload all company data in case it is useful
Upload only the data the task needs and make sure that sharing it with the agent is allowed
exp: Data minimization and checking that personal data may be used protect privacy while still letting the agent do the analysis. Uploading everything increases exposure, content filters are a safety layer that should stay on, and sharing conversations publicly can leak personal data.

q: In a client app, which value tells the SDK which agent to talk to?
opts: The font of the chat window
exp: The client passes the agent's name, for example to get_openai_client(agent_name=...), so requests go to that agent. The tenant ID, storage keys and fonts do not identify an agent.

q: After a page reload, a web client must show the user's earlier messages with an agent. What should it do?
opts: Keep the conversation ID and list the conversation's items to rebuild the history
Ask the user to type everything again
exp: Conversations are stored by the service, so the client can save the conversation ID, for example in the user's session, and list its items to redisplay the history. A new agent knows nothing about the old chat, asking users to retype is poor design, and instructions do not contain chat history.

q: For each of the following statements about agent clients, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: A client must use the same programming language that was used to create the agent.
One agent can serve many different client apps.
Agents can be called from Python, C#, JavaScript or the REST API.
exp: No for the first: the agent lives in Foundry, so any supported SDK or plain REST calls can use it. Yes for the second: a web app, a mobile app and a Teams bot can all talk to the same agent. Yes for the third: SDKs exist for several languages, and REST works from anywhere.

q: The agent is named faq-bot. Complete the Python code that asks it a question.
exp: The client is bound to the agent by its name, faq-bot, and the input is the user's question. gpt-5-mini is a model name and eastus is a region, not the agent. temperature is a parameter name and 429 is an error code, so neither is a question.

q: Match each client task to the call that performs it. Each call can be used once or not at all.
items: Start a new chat
Send the next user message
Remove a finished chat
Talk to a specific agent
exp: conversations.create() starts a chat, responses.create() with the conversation ID sends each message, conversations.delete() removes a finished chat, and get_openai_client(agent_name=...) targets a specific agent. images.generate() creates images and is not part of chatting with an agent.

q: Which THREE practices make an agent client app secure? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Put the project endpoint and a key in a public web page
Authenticate to Foundry with Microsoft Entra ID
Log full conversations, including any passwords users type
Make sure each user can access only their own conversations
Call the agent from a backend, not from the browser
exp: Entra ID avoids exposed secrets, ownership checks keep chats private, and a backend keeps credentials away from the browser. A key in a public page can be copied by anyone, and logged passwords can leak.

q: Put the steps of one chat session in an agent client in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Delete the conversation when the session ends
Delete the agent
Get a client that is bound to the agent
Send messages with responses.create() and the conversation ID
Create a conversation
exp: The client is bound to the agent first, a conversation is created for the session, each message is sent with that conversation ID, and the conversation can be deleted when the session ends. Deleting the agent would break it for every other user.

q: TextAnalyticsClient needs the endpoint of which kind of resource?
opts: An Azure Language resource, or a Microsoft Foundry resource that includes Language
exp: Azure Language features are served by a Language resource or by a multi-service Foundry resource, and the client uses that resource's endpoint. Storage accounts, virtual networks and SQL databases do not host text analysis.

q: A support app must detect unhappy messages and draft an empathetic reply for each one. Which design fits?
opts: Generate replies for every message first, then analyze the sentiment of the replies
Analyze sentiment with Azure Language, then send the negative messages with clear instructions to a chat model to draft replies
Turn every message into an image
exp: Sentiment analysis cheaply finds the negative messages, and a chat model with instructions writes suitable replies only for those. Analyzing the replies instead of the customer messages misses the goal, and OCR or images are irrelevant for text messages.

q: For each of the following statements about text analysis apps, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: You can use prebuilt sentiment analysis without training any model.
Azure Language features are called over HTTPS.
Text analysis results can be stored in a database for reporting.
exp: Yes for the first: prebuilt features work immediately; training is only for custom features. Yes for the second: the SDKs call the service's HTTPS endpoint. Yes for the third: results such as sentiment and key phrases are data that can feed dashboards.

q: Complete the Python code that prints abstractive summaries of documents.
exp: begin_abstract_summary() returns a poller, and result() waits for the operation and returns the document results. Each result has a list of summaries whose text property holds the summary. wait() and done() do not return results, and sentiment and category belong to other features.

q: Which TWO practices make a text analysis app more efficient? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Call the API once for every word
Send documents in batches instead of one request per sentence
Analyze unchanged documents again every minute
Request several analyses in one job when you need them together
exp: Batching documents and combining analyses into one job reduce the number of calls and overhead. Calling per word, reanalyzing unchanged text and sending images instead of text waste requests or do not work at all.

q: What is a key benefit of letting users ask questions with spoken prompts?
opts: Users can ask questions hands-free, which also improves accessibility
The app works without any internet connection
exp: Speaking is hands-free and helps people who find typing difficult, which makes the app more accessible. Requests are still billed, a model is still needed to understand and answer, and cloud models need a network connection.

ctx: Field technicians wear gloves and record voice questions on a tablet. The answers must be played back to them as audio.
q: Which single-model approach fits?
opts: A text-only model without any speech service
An audio-capable chat model that accepts the recording and returns spoken audio
exp: An audio-capable chat model can take the recorded question and return audio, so one model handles both understanding and the spoken reply. Embedding and image models do not answer questions, and a text-only model would need separate speech services.

q: For each of the following statements about spoken prompts, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Background noise reduces the quality of answers to spoken prompts.
Spoken prompts cannot be combined with conversation history.
A spoken prompt can include instructions such as 'answer briefly'.
exp: Yes for the first: noisy audio makes the question harder to understand. No for the second: audio turns can be part of a conversation with earlier messages. Yes for the third: spoken requests can contain instructions just like typed ones.

q: In a voice app built from separate services, match each step to the component that performs it. Each component can be used once or not at all.
items: Turn the user's recording into text
Write the answer
Turn the answer into audio
exp: Speech to text transcribes the question, a chat model writes the answer and text to speech speaks it. Image Analysis works on pictures and has no role in this pipeline. An audio-capable model can replace these three steps with one request.

q: Which Speech SDK method recognizes a single utterance and then stops?
exp: recognize_once_async() listens until one utterance ends and returns its result. speak_text_async() synthesizes speech, analyze_sentiment() belongs to the Language SDK, and responses.create() calls a language model.

q: A subtitle app needs the time at which each word was spoken. What should it enable in the Speech SDK?
opts: Word-level timestamps, for example by calling request_word_level_timestamps() on the SpeechConfig
exp: Requesting word-level timestamps adds the offset and duration of each recognized word to the detailed results, which is what subtitles need. Voices and SSML affect synthesized speech, and text analytics does not deal with audio timing.

q: For each of the following statements about the Speech SDK, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The Speech SDK covers speech to text, while text to speech needs a different SDK.
Speech translation in the SDK is limited to one target language per request.
The Speech SDK can be used only from C#.
exp: No for the first: recognizers and synthesizers are both part of the Speech SDK. No for the second: you can call add_target_language() several times to get several translations at once. No for the third: the SDK is available for Python, C#, Java, JavaScript and other languages.

q: Complete the sentences about the Speech SDK.
tpl: To listen to the microphone and get text, create a {0}. To speak text aloud, create a {1}.
exp: SpeechRecognizer turns audio into text, and SpeechSynthesizer turns text into audio. TextAnalyticsClient belongs to Azure Language and analyzes text, so it neither listens nor speaks.

q: You are building a simple voice chatbot with the Speech SDK and a chat model. Put the steps of one turn in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Speak the model's answer with SpeechSynthesizer
Run image analysis on the question
Recognize the user's question with SpeechRecognizer
Wait for the next question
Send the recognized text to the chat model
exp: Each turn recognizes the spoken question, sends the text to the chat model, speaks the answer and then waits for the next question. Image analysis has nothing to analyze in a voice-only conversation.
